findings: Round-3 capped fix cycle for design 87. Both Majors ADOPTED, neither appealed; all 3 Minors folded; Q7 ruling folded; document at rev 3, commit 2ade67fb7747b55cecc51ad18d0d78f1b530018a, plus 295 minus 82 over rev 2's 3c31ed0. Section 5.5 now carries a three-population table (six fossil manifests, every Copilot in-flight dispatch LIVE and PERMANENT, every presumed-lost record) and calls the clause STRUCTURAL rather than legacy; Q4 is CLOSED with its defective cost basis kept visible rather than quietly restated, because a soft-spot question priced wrongly routes a reviewer or owner to a wrong decision and that is worse than no question; section 7's minted-id stamping row is RETIRED not re-triggered, since rev 2 gated it on a D8 landing that section 5.7 says never happens for that family, which made the clause permanent by construction rather than by decision. abstract: Round-3 revision, the capped round, of the manifest member identity design for issue 87, folding the round-2 delta REJECT of 2 Major and 3 Minor. Committed at 2ade67fb7747b55cecc51ad18d0d78f1b530018a over rev 2 at 3c31ed0, one file, plus 295 minus 82, nothing pushed and no board file edited. Both Majors were defects the round-2 fixes themselves created, which is why this rung is capped, and both are adopted without appeal. The first is a characterization that my own per-family rewrite had silently falsified: the join's second clause, described throughout as serving six fossil manifests, is in fact the permanent binding path for a live runtime family every time it dispatches, and one open question was inviting the reviewer to delete it on that false basis. The clause is now called structural, the question is closed with its defective pricing left visible rather than quietly restated, and an out-of-scope row that would have retired the clause by construction is itself retired. Following that correction past the finding exposed a binding path that crosses the rule's two clauses and that no conformance vector reached, so one is added. The second Major is a vector introduced last round that forbade an operation byte-for-byte indistinguishable from one it permits; rather than find it an enforcer, the clause is deleted, on the grounds that the precedence rule already guards what it was protecting, that the forbidden operation's outcome is honest anyway, and that a gate with nothing to catch is a pruning candidate by this repo's own doctrine. The alternative is named and declined for a stated reason and the removal is routed to a new open question, because this is the one place the revision removes a rule rather than adding one. Three Minors close an overstated coverage claim, a record schema whose field description the proposed wire falsifies twice, and an unasked question about the shape of what gets stamped. The reviewer's wire-shape ruling is folded as a decision with its carry named. Two defects were caught by the author rather than any gate, one of them a consequence the Major's own fix falsified one section over, which is the same class the cap exists to detect and was found by turning the check inward before shipping.
